title: Surviving a Provider Transition
description: When a contract changes hands, knowledge walks out the door. Drawing on LA County's 2024 transition, this workshop covers knowledge transfer, caseload handoff, onboarding a new provider's staff, and protecting performance data during the gap.
notes: Audience: Board staff, incoming and outgoing providers. Format: HD. Hours assumed from format (HD = 4 hours).
learning_objectives: Build a transition plan covering caseloads, files, open contracts, and data entry.
Identify the performance indicators most at risk during a transition.
Set up a rapid onboarding sequence for incoming staff.
Write transition and knowledge-transfer requirements into RFPs and contracts.

sequencing_rationale: Lessons follow the catalog's learning objectives in the order a practitioner meets them on the job: Building the Transition Plan; Performance Indicators Most at Risk; Rapid Onboarding for Incoming Staff; Writing Transition Requirements into RFPs and Contracts. The closing project ("Project: Transition Tabletop Exercise") applies the earlier lessons to one realistic work product (a provider transition plan with an at-risk indicator analysis, an onboarding sequence, and RFP or contract transition language) rather than introducing new content. Scope assumptions: hours are not stated in the source catalog and are assumed from the delivery format (HD; HD = 4 hours). Content is grounded in California and federal guidance named in the catalog description and objectives; the course cites those directives by number but does not reproduce their text, and every policy-specific claim must be checked against the current directive before delivery. Local board policy is treated as a variable the learner fills in from their own board, not something the course prescribes.
